notes: Gzip-9 bytes of each Web-facing entry as scripts/bundle-size.mjs bundles it. baselineGzip is the P1-S19 measurement at 0.25.0, with the Effect core in place; main before the conversion (4f536a8) was 235,346 B at the root and 263,949 B for the Worker example.

Caps: every capped entry gets baseline + 60,000 B. The conversion-era allowances are retired: the root's flat 386,000 B cap covered a rewrite that is finished, and the +160 KB held for HttpApi in ./ui, ./activity and the Worker example was never spent, because P1-S18 measured HttpApi and did not use it.

Per-provider entries (./providers/*) are reported, not capped (decision 0009, #898). Every deployment imports the root, which already carries the Effect core, so a provider's standalone bundle bills it again for code the deployment pays for once. Hard gzip caps stay on the deployed shapes: the root, ./worker, ./ui, operator-ui/assets, ./d1, ./auth/access-tokens and examples/worker, along with the remaining non-provider entries. A provider's growth shows in review as its Δ against baselineGzip and in the src column of its row, not as a failure. Provider definitions keep baselineGzip so the report still prints each provider's size and its Δ, and scripts/bundle-size.mjs refuses a cap on a provider entry. The same change pins effect to exactly 4.0.5 (from ^4.0.0 resolving 4.0.0); against main at c7370c68 on the same machine that adds 967 B gzip to the root (378,203 B to 379,170 B), 907 B to ./ui, 915 B to ./worker and 1,020 B to examples/worker (719,163 B to 720,183 B). No cap moves.
A cap moves only in a change that says why. Raising one to make a check pass is the failure this file exists to catch.

The growth comes from B.1's call-service and lifetime architecture plus review rounds 2-5: fail-closed copies, revocation, request-signal binding, signal-raced pre-claim grant reads and the round-5 settleOnClose boundary helper at every entry point. Always use CI's measured number. All baselines and other caps stay unchanged.

The index was shrunk before its former cap moved, from 157 KB to 125 KB gzip as source: request details to depth 2 without descriptions or enums over 50 values, no operation ids (they restate summaries), no plain-string path parameters (the template names them), and a 6,000-character per-operation budget that lowers one sprawling operation's depth. Depth 1 would save about 18 KB more at the cost of nested validation such as DNS record alternatives. Removing 23 hand-written reads offsets part of the growth; the reviewed value-safety table adds about 12 KB. The value-safety consolidation (#801) moved the spec-derived candidate record out of the index and grew the table by 259 verdicts, a net +3,646 B (337,701 B), inside its former cap.
